summary: A Yes vote amends Oakland's Real Property Transfer Tax to eliminate the foreclosure exemption for most transfers, with specified exceptions, and lets the City Council set foreclosure-related exceptions, raising about $4 million to $13 million annually beginning January 1, 2027 until repealed.

tax.text: A Yes vote would remove foreclosure exemptions from Oakland’s real property transfer tax for most commercial and multifamily properties and raise revenue for the city’s General Fund.
tax.quote: generating approximately $4 million to $13 million annually in revenue to bolster the city’s General Fund over the next five years.

tax.text: A No vote would reject Measure FF, which would extend Oakland’s real property transfer tax to most foreclosed commercial and multifamily properties.
tax.quote: The measure would eliminate an exemption from Oakland’s real property transfer tax for most foreclosed commercial and multifamily residential properties
